newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cultus says Cornea evaluation starts.
newsitem.headline: Cultus says Cornea evaluation starts.

text.p: Co-venturers in the Cornea oil and gas discovery in the Browse Basin offshore Western Australia will begin a drilling programme to determine the extent of the field on Saturday, Cultus Petroleum NL said on Friday.
A total of 11 wells are planned up to July 1998 when processing of raw data from a 3D-seismic survey is also expected to be completed, Cultus said.

"At the end of this evaluation process, the joint venture will be in a position to estimate preliminary recoverable reserves and to have an understanding as to the likely productivity of the Cornea reservoirs," Cultus said in a
Cultus, through subsidiary Basin Oil NL, has a 25 percent stake in permit WA-241-P, where the Cornea-1 wildcat well made an oil and gas find, announced in January.
Operator Royal Dutch/Shell unit Shell Development Australia has 50 percent and Chevron Corp unit Chevron Asiatic Ltd 25 percent.

Cultus said in May the field could contain between 617 million and 2,665 million barrels of oil, although Shell said later the recovery rate could be as low as five percent, with something in the range of five to 35 percent likely.
Cultus said on Friday the Cornea South-1 well would spudded about five km east of Cornea-1, on or about August 2.
Cultus warned the success or failure of individual wells may not determine recoverable reserves at Cornea or whether it is commercial.
It also said future reporting by Cultus would be limited to recoverable reserves, rather than "in place" estimations.
